title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
gist: Danijar Hafner, 31, left Google DeepMind in fall 2025 to found a stealth San Francisco robotics startup built on his world-model/model-based reinforcement-learning research (PlaNet, Dreamer series, DayDreamer), importing Chinese-made humanoid robots to embody agents that can plan ahead in never-before-seen environments without real-world trial-and-error training.

themes.theme: Stealth startup and its bet on world models

insights.claim: Danijar Hafner left Google DeepMind in the fall of 2025 to found a new stealth-mode humanoid-robotics startup in San Francisco's SoMa district that has not yet disclosed its name, is applying his world-model research to physical robots, and imports its humanoid hardware from China rather than building it in-house.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: A well-regarded ex-DeepMind researcher building on imported Chinese humanoid hardware (rather than in-house robots) signals the humanoid supply chain from China is now considered good enough for US AI-robotics startups to build software-first on top of, rather than vertically integrate — watch for a funding round disclosure and for who the hardware supplier is.
insights.quote: Today, Hafner is working on his new startup, which he left Google DeepMind to form in the fall of 2025.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Today, Hafner is working on his new startup'

insights.claim: Hafner's core technical approach is model-based reinforcement learning: he builds 'world models' — AI systems that emulate physical reality — and trains agents inside them so the agents can simulate and predict future outcomes ('dream' or imagine) before acting, letting robots handle situations never seen in training.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: World-model-based RL is positioned as a capital-efficient alternative to the expensive real-world trial-and-error data collection that dominates current robotics training pipelines (e.g., Tesla Optimus, Figure) — a differentiator to check against competitors' training-data cost structures.
insights.quote: He develops world models—AI models designed to emulate physical reality—and trains agents within them.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'To achieve this, Hafner relies on'

insights.claim: Unlike conventional robotics approaches, Hafner's technique lets agents and the robots controlling them execute highly complex tasks without the extensive real-world trial-and-error training traditionally required in robotics.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: If world-model training genuinely reduces reliance on costly real-world robot data collection, it undercuts the moat that data-rich robotics incumbents are trying to build — worth stress-testing against Hafner's new startup's actual demos once it exits stealth.
insights.quote: Unlike other efforts, Hafner’s technique enables agents and the robots they control to execute massively complicated tasks without the real-world trial-and-­error training that’s traditionally been used in robotics.

insights.claim: The generalization goal is explicitly household deployment: for a robot to be useful in a person's home it must handle floor plans and furniture configurations it has never encountered, which Hafner frames as the key unsolved capability gate for getting robots into human spaces.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: Frames the addressable market explicitly as in-home consumer/service robotics, not just industrial/warehouse robotics — relevant for sizing which robotics investment thesis (consumer vs. industrial) Hafner's startup will target.
insights.quote: Because if you want to send a robot into a person’s home, for example, it needs to be able to handle a floor plan and furniture it’s never seen before.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'The humanoids, which he imports from China'

themes.theme: Track record: Dreamer lineage as proof points

insights.claim: Hafner's PlaNet model was his first breakthrough, letting agents act by planning ahead; Dreamer 2 was the first agent to reach human-level performance on Atari 2600 games using a world model; Dreamer 3 was the first to solve the Minecraft Diamond challenge (mining diamonds autonomously); and Dreamer 4 went further by learning to mine diamonds purely from an offline dataset of recorded gameplay video, without ever interacting with the game directly.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: A four-generation public track record of solving progressively harder benchmarks (including learning entirely offline from video, i.e., no environment interaction) is unusually strong technical diligence evidence for an early-stage robotics bet — rare for a pre-product-launch stealth startup.
insights.quote: Dreamer 3 was the first one to solve the Minecraft Diamond challenge—successfully mining in-game gems on its own. And Dreamer 4 went a step beyond that by learning to mine diamonds from an offline data set of recorded game-play videos, without ever interacting with the game directly.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Over the years, Hafner has honed'

insights.claim: Hafner's DayDreamer project used the Dreamer algorithm to let physical robots operate in novel environments and react to new, unplanned experiences (such as being pushed over) without task-specific training, marking his transition from purely virtual game environments into physical-world robotics.
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: DayDreamer is the direct technical precursor to the new startup's humanoid work — investors diligencing the new company should look at DayDreamer's published results as the closest available proxy for what the stealth product can currently do.
insights.quote: His DayDreamer project used the Dreamer algorithm to let robots operate themselves in novel environments and react to new experiences (such as being pushed over) without any specific training.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'More recently, he's begun to migrate'

insights.claim: Timothy Lillicrap, a former manager and coauthor of Hafner's at Google, rates him in roughly the top half of one percent of researchers he has worked with and says Hafner has single-handedly built things that would normally take entire engineering teams.
insights.speaker: Timothy Lillicrap, Google DeepMind
insights.so_what: Strong, named third-party technical endorsement from a senior DeepMind researcher is a soft signal worth weighing in early-stage diligence when there is no product yet to evaluate directly.
insights.quote: I get to interact with a lot of really smart people in research at Google, and he easily sits in the top half of 1%.
insights.locator: Pull quote attributed to Timothy Lillicrap

insights.claim: Hafner worked as a student researcher and later intern/staff across a dozen roles at Google Brain and Google DeepMind (UK, Canada, US) starting in 2015 as a second-year undergraduate at Hasso Plattner Institute, working alongside Geoffrey Hinton and Ashish Vaswani (coauthor of 'Attention Is All You Need').
insights.speaker: Mat Honan
insights.so_what: A roughly decade-long research pedigree spanning the transformer-era godfathers of AI at Google is a strong recruiting and credibility signal for the stealth startup's eventual funding pitch.
insights.quote: In 2015, as a second-year under­graduate studying engineering at Hasso Plattner Institute in Potsdam, he won a role as a student researcher at Google Brain.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Hafner grew up in a rural town'
